stories.title: More than 5,000 deaths in DRC's deadliest Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: More than 5,000 people have died in the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to government data. The outbreak began in May, became the country’s deadliest in August, and currently has a case‑fatality rate of 48.6%, with the epicentre in the conflict‑affected Ituri province. It is the 17th Ebola outbreak recorded in the country and the second largest worldwide.
stories.why: The high death toll and spread in a conflict zone raise regional health risks and make containment harder.

stories.title: Turnaround Story: 8 stocks shift from loss to profit in September '26 quarter
stories.summary: The company reported a net profit of Rs 859 crore in the September 2026 quarter, compared with a net loss of Rs 16 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The firm posted a net profit of Rs 71 crore in the September 2026 quarter, against a net loss of Rs 10 crore in the year-ago quarter.

stories.title: Judge denies xAI motion to dismiss NAACP data‑center emissions lawsuit
stories.summary: A federal judge denied xAI’s request to dismiss a lawsuit filed by the NAACP and the Southern Environmental Law Center, which alleges the SpaceX‑owned company operated at least 35 combustion turbines at its Colossus data center outside Memphis without required pre‑construction or operating air permits, violating the Clean Air Act. The court held that the plaintiffs have statutory standing and that the turbines are not “mobile sources” under Mississippi law, so the case will move forward.
stories.why: The ruling lets the plaintiffs pursue their claims that the data center may have breached air‑pollution permitting rules.

stories.previousSummary: A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis. xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile.
